verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean keeps the two angular terms the paper deletes. Lean's remainder is r_m = curlRemainder K R Vr Vθ Vz (coefficient …) = (i/K)·curl_*(coefficient); since C_m = (i/K)·coefficient and the scalar i/K is constant in x, cylindricalCurl_const_smul (line 389, needing differentiability of the coefficient components) turns this into curl_* C_m, i.e. the full three components of (7.37) applied to C_m: ( R^{-1}∂_θ(C_m)_z − D_z(C_m)_θ, D_z(C_m)_r − D_r(C_m)_z, (D_r+R^{-1})(C_m)_θ − R^{-1}∂_θ(C_m)_r ). The paper's display drops the two R^{-1}∂_θ terms, justified in the sentence before it ("Since C_m is independent of θ"). Under that same θ-independence the two expressions agree term by term, signs and the R^{-1} connection term included; Lean carries the θ-independence as a separate hypothesis/lemma (AngularIndependent, CopyAngularInvariance.coefficient_invariant) rather than folding it into the formula, and I found no declaration stating the θ-stripped three-component form itself. No constant, exponent, sign or derivative count differs.
